channel.title: AAT University News & Announcements
channel.description: The latest news, official announcements and academic developments from AbdulRasaq Abubakar Toyin University.

item.title: NOTICE TO ALL FRESH STUDENTS
item.description: Academic activities resume on Friday, 30 October 2026, while clearance activities begin on Monday, 2 November 2026.

item.title: Vice-Chancellor schedules visits to faculties, directorates and units
item.description: The two-day schedule covers the University’s faculties on 20 October and directorates and service units on 21 October 2026.

item.title: Guidance for candidates on verifying admission information
item.description: Candidates are encouraged to confirm programme availability, requirements and application details directly with the Admissions Office.

item.title: 2026/2027 undergraduate admission exercise now open
item.description: Prospective candidates can now review entry requirements, available programmes and the application guidance for the new session.

item.title: Admission requirements for the 2026/2027 session
item.description: A summary of UTME and Direct Entry requirements, alongside the full list of programmes available across the university.

item.title: Professor Olayemi Mikail Olaniyi appointed first substantive Vice-Chancellor
item.description: The appointment takes effect from 4 September 2026 and marks a new chapter in the university’s academic development.

item.title: AATU signs Beyond Benign Green Chemistry Commitment
item.description: The commitment places the University among more than 300 institutions worldwide advancing safer, more sustainable chemistry education.

item.title: Additional 15 undergraduate programmes approved for 2026/2027
item.description: The newly approved programmes expand AATU’s academic portfolio across law, health sciences, computing and the social sciences.

item.title: Campus facilities take shape ahead of academic take-off
item.description: Teaching spaces, library resources, laboratories and computing facilities have been developed to support the university’s academic programmes.
